how.label: How Voxtera works

faq.label: Questions, briefly answered
faq.title: Things people always ask.
faq.q1: How fast is the response, really?
faq.a1: End-to-end — from the moment the guest stops speaking to the first syllable of Voxtera's reply — averages 600 to 850 milliseconds. That's faster than most human pickups on a hotel phone, and well within the threshold where conversation feels natural.
faq.a2: Voxtera stops immediately, listens, and continues the new thread — like a real conversation, not a robocall menu.
faq.q3: How does it know about my property?
faq.a3: During onboarding we ingest your menus, room amenities, hours, house rules, local recommendations and FAQs into a private knowledge layer. Updates take seconds — change your spa hours and Voxtera knows on the next call.
faq.q4: What about escalating to a real person?
faq.a4: Anything safety-related, medical, or emotionally distressed is flagged in real time and routed to a staff member via the channel you specify — Slack, SMS, internal phone. Voxtera stays with the guest until the handover completes.
faq.a5: Infrastructure is deployed in the region closest to your property — North America, Europe, or other regions as needed. We work with trusted subprocessors and select hosting regions per deployment. Full details on data routing and subprocessors are available on request. All conversations are encrypted in transit and at rest; recordings can be disabled per-property.
faq.q6: Can it handle a phone line, not just web?
faq.a6: Yes. We'll work with you to connect Voxtera to your existing phone system — so the same brain, the same voices, and the same languages reach every guest who calls in.
faq.q7: Can it connect to the systems we already use?
faq.a7: Yes. Voxtera can connect to your management system and open customer tickets automatically — or route every guest request straight to your team's Telegram, WhatsApp, or Slack. Your staff stay in the tools they already know.

cb.uc_label: Five ways Voxtera + Cloudbeds work together
cb.uc_title:
One integration.
Five quiet improvements —
every day, every guest.
cb.uc_intro: Each of these uses the Cloudbeds API or webhooks in a specific way. None of them require a new app, a new screen, or a new login for your team. They just happen.
cb.uc1_tag: getAvailableRoomTypes · getRatePlans · push to Telegram or WhatsApp · WhatsApp confirmation
cb.uc1_scenario: 11:48pm. A French couple calls about a sea-view room next weekend. Voxtera detects French on the first syllable, quotes live availability from your Cloudbeds — $240/night, breakfast included, two rooms left — and asks for their name and email. By the time your reservations manager opens Telegram or WhatsApp at 8am, the lead is waiting with a recording, transcript, and a one-tap "confirm booking" button.
cb.uc1_b1: After-hours booking calls are your highest-intent inbound traffic — direct, not OTA
cb.uc1_b2: Boutiques lose an estimated 30–60% of these calls today; you can't measure what you can't capture
cb.uc1_b3: Voxtera writes the call as a structured note on a new Cloudbeds guest profile, so even uncaptured leads aren't lost
cb.uc1_b4: One recovered booking per month pays Voxtera back roughly twice over at $200–400/night
cb.uc1_limit: Voxtera captures the lead. It does not auto-create confirmed reservations — your team approves each one in the morning. The conversion from warm lead to actual booking depends on how fast your reservations team replies; we recommend within 12 hours.
cb.uc2_tag: getReservations (arriving / in-house / departing within 7 days) · guest profile lookup by phone
cb.uc2_scenario: Mr. Müller, currently in room 207, calls from his mobile. Voxtera matches the number to his active Cloudbeds reservation in under a second, greets him by name in German, and already knows his room number and his note about a previous late checkout. He asks about extending one night; Voxtera quotes the rate from live availability and creates a tentative request for your front desk.
cb.uc2_b1: No more "what room are you calling from?" misheard through an accent
cb.uc2_b2: The guest feels recognized from word one — the boutique difference, automated
cb.uc2_b3: Conversation context (room, language, VIP status, prior notes) is attached to every ticket the call generates
cb.uc2_limit: Recognition only works when the caller's number matches the one in their Cloudbeds profile. International SIMs, family-member phones, and front-desk-collected numbers that staff forgot to log will fall back to "may I have your booking name?" gracefully. Realistic match rate is around 60–70% for active in-house guests, lower pre-arrival.
cb.uc3_tag: postGuestNote · webhook write-back · rule-based urgency → priority routing
cb.uc3_scenario: Brazilian family in room 412 calls reception at 23:51: the AC isn't cooling and the baby is crying. Voxtera classifies the request as urgent based on category ("AC failure") and hour (after 22:00), tags the ticket accordingly, posts it in Portuguese to the maintenance Telegram group with a 15-minute SLA, and pings the duty manager. If no one acknowledges within 15 minutes, the on-call number gets a voice call. Once resolved, Voxtera sends the guest a WhatsApp confirmation in Portuguese: "Quarto 412 — ar-condicionado reparado. Boa noite."
cb.uc3_b1: Maintenance complaints after 22:00 escalate before a guest gives up and writes a bad review
cb.uc3_b2: Routine daytime requests (towels, late checkout, breakfast question) flow through the same pipeline without paging anyone urgently
cb.uc3_b3: Every ticket — routine or urgent — gets written as a structured note on the guest's Cloudbeds profile, so next time they book your front desk sees the history
cb.uc3_b4: The audit trail your insurer, brand standards or owner asks for, without anyone manually logging
cb.uc3_limit: Urgency is determined by rules — request category, hour of day, keywords like "broken," "emergency," "leaking," "medical." Voxtera does not analyze voice tone or detect emotion. A guest who calmly asks about a broken AC at 3pm will be classified routine; the same call at 2am will be urgent. The thresholds are tunable per property after the pilot.
cb.uc3_status: Routine ticketing live · category-and-time-based urgency in beta · SLA-driven escalation Q3 2026
cb.uc4_tag: webhook reservation/confirmed · guest language · WhatsApp Business template
cb.uc4_scenario: Mrs. Tanaka books your hotel through a Japanese OTA. 48 hours before arrival, Cloudbeds fires the confirmation webhook. Voxtera sends her one WhatsApp message in Japanese: check-in time, the property address with a Google Maps link, the wifi network, breakfast hours, and a single sentence — "Reply to this message if you need anything before you arrive." That's it. No promotional content, no upsell. Just the information your front desk would have called or emailed her anyway, delivered in her language, on the channel she actually reads.
cb.uc4_b1: Cuts inbound "what time is check-in?" / "where exactly is the hotel?" calls by 30–50% in pilot data
cb.uc4_b2: Guests in non-English-speaking countries especially appreciate practical info in their language — most boutiques send English-only emails
cb.uc4_b3: One pre-approved WhatsApp template per property; you write the template once, Voxtera fills in the variables
cb.uc4_b4: Stays strictly within WhatsApp Business's transactional-message rules — no promotional opt-in headaches
cb.uc4_limit: WhatsApp requires the guest's mobile number in Cloudbeds. Booking via OTA channels that don't share phone numbers (common with Booking.com) means the guest won't get the message — they'll get your existing email confirmation only.
cb.uc5_tag: getReservations (checked-out, last 7 days) · postGuestNote · WhatsApp follow-up
cb.uc5_scenario: Mr. Rossi calls the hotel from the airport in panic — his passport is in the room safe and his flight to Milan boards in three hours. Voxtera doesn't recognize the number (his Italian SIM, not the one in his booking); he gives his name and check-out date in Italian. Voxtera matches the reservation, logs the case as urgent against his guest profile, pings the duty manager directly on Telegram with the room number and the time pressure, and confirms to Mr. Rossi in Italian that the front desk has been alerted and will call him back in five minutes. A real human takes it from there — but the right human, with the right context, in under a minute.
cb.uc5_b1: Forgotten passports, jewelry from the safe, wallets, prescription medication — these are the calls that actually come in, and they're high-stress for both guest and staff
cb.uc5_b2: Voxtera's job here is triage and context, not resolution: get the right reservation in front of the right manager fast, in the guest's language, with the guest already calmed
cb.uc5_b3: Every case is logged as a structured note on the guest's Cloudbeds profile — owner gets a real lost-property log instead of a chat history nobody can search
cb.uc5_b4: Recovering a passport in someone's language earns the kind of post-stay review boutiques can't buy
cb.uc5_limit: Voxtera handles the intake and routing. The actual item recovery, the courier arrangement, the conversation with the airline — that's a human job, and should be. The value of this card is that your team gets the call routed to them already structured, not that the bot solves the crisis alone.
cb.int_label: What we read. What we write.
cb.int_intro: We're not a black box. Here's exactly what Voxtera reads from your Cloudbeds account, and exactly what it writes back. Nothing more, nothing less.
cb.int_read_b1: Reservations (current, arriving, departing, checked-out within 7 days)
cb.int_read_b2: Guest profiles, languages, special requests, VIP status
cb.int_read_b5: Webhooks: created, confirmed, checked-in, checked-out, room-changed, cancelled
cb.int_write_b4: Optional: tentative reservations from booking calls (pending your staff confirmation)
cb.int_write_b5: Optional: post-stay sentiment tags from outbound check-out call
cb.int_never_1: We never access — credit card data, payment methods, financial reports
cb.int_never_2: We never create — confirmed bookings without your staff approval
cb.int_never_3: We never delete — reservations, notes, profiles. Voxtera is additive, not destructive.

cb.faq_q1: Do we need a specific Cloudbeds plan?
cb.faq_a1: Any Cloudbeds plan with API access works. Some Cloudbeds tiers include API access at no extra cost; some charge for it. We'll help you check during onboarding. If your plan requires an upgrade for API access, we'll tell you before you commit to Voxtera.
cb.faq_a2: A typical install takes under an hour. You authorize Voxtera in your Cloudbeds account (one click), tell us which Telegram or WhatsApp group your team uses, and we provision a phone number. Most properties are live the same day.
cb.faq_q3: What happens if Cloudbeds goes down?
cb.faq_a3: Voxtera still answers calls. It will tell guests we're unable to access reservations momentarily, and queue all tickets for your team in Telegram. Once Cloudbeds is back, queued notes and tickets sync automatically. Voxtera is never a single point of failure for your phone line.
cb.faq_q4: Will my staff need to learn anything new?
cb.faq_a4: No. That's the whole point. Voxtera posts into the Telegram, WhatsApp or Slack group your team already uses. The only difference your staff notices is more requests show up pre-tagged with room number, language, and priority.
cb.faq_q5: What about guests who want a human?
cb.faq_a5: Anyone asks for a person, they get a person. We route the call to whatever phone number you specify — front desk, night manager, on-call. No escalation gauntlets. No "are you sure?" loops.
cb.faq_q6: Is our guest data sold or used to train models?
cb.faq_a6: No. Guest conversations are never used for training, never shared with third parties, and stored only as long as needed for your operations and audit. Full DPA available on request.
cb.faq_q7: Can we try it before paying?
cb.faq_a7: Yes. 30-day pilot on any tier, no card required upfront. If at the end of 30 days it isn't earning its $200/month back, you walk away — and we'll send you the conversation logs and ticket history as a parting gift.
cb.faq_q8: Do you support Cloudbeds-connected door locks?
cb.faq_a8: On the roadmap. Today Voxtera doesn't generate or distribute mobile keys — we keep that securely in Cloudbeds and your door lock vendor. We can announce a room-ready key over voice or WhatsApp once Cloudbeds fires the room-assignment webhook.
